scenes.narration: Inside every AI are billions of tiny dials.
Welcome to FredsDesk, lesson seven. In under a minute, you'll learn what parameters are.
Parameters are the numbers inside a model that training adjusts. Together, they hold everything the model has learned.
scenes.definition: The adjustable numbers inside a model that hold what it learned.

scenes.narration: Picture a mixing board in a music studio. With a few knobs, you get a simple sound. With thousands, you can shape almost any sound. Parameters are the model's knobs.
Here's the journey. A new model starts with random settings. Training turns every knob a little, again and again. When it's done, the final values are saved, and that saved file is the model.
Large language models have billions of parameters. More can mean more skill, but it also costs more to train and run.
scenes.label: Parameters in a large model
scenes.sub: Each one is just a number.
scenes.note: More knobs, more skill, more cost

scenes.narration: Quick recap. One: parameters are the numbers inside a model. Two: training tunes them. Three: more parameters can mean more skill, at a higher cost.
points: More can mean more skill, more cost
